newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HIH WINTERTHUR EYES RATINGS UPGRADE.
newsitem.headline: HIH WINTERTHUR EYES RATINGS UPGRADE.

text.p: Sydney-based insurer HIH Winterthur International Holdings said on Tuesday the planned merger of parent Winterthur Group with Credit Suisse Group may increase its claims paying rating.

"Assuming it goes through, the only possible ramification could be an even further strengthening of our claims paying ability rating of AA-minus," HIH Winterthur spokesman John Clarke said. HIH Winterthur is 51 percent owned by Winterthur.
Credit Suisse has an AA rating from Standard and Poors and a A1 senior debt rating from Moody's Investors Service.
Earlier on Tuesday Moody's affirmed the Winterthur group's AA3 senior guaranteed debt rating, but Standard & Poor's has yet to revise the group's claims paying ability rating.
Credit Suisse and Winterthur Group on Monday announced plans to merge.
The merger catapults Credit Suisse Group into the position of undisputed leader among Switzerland's Big Three Banks.
The new entity will have shareholder equity of around 23 billion Swiss francs (US$15 billion) and assets of around 700 billion francs (US$463 billion).
"It means that our major shareholder becomes a so much larger international group which strengthens our position," Clarke said.
"Because Credit Suisse don't have any significant insurance operations, Winterthur's operations will operate independently," he said.
"That being the case, one would believe it would not affect our operations," he said.
